## Highlights

**Unpinned `runner_version` now tracks the latest actions/runner release.**

ghars registers runners with `--disableupdate`, making ghars the fleet's only
upgrade path. Previously, a runner deployed without a pinned `runner_version`
froze at whatever release was current at create time, and `plan` reported
"in sync" indefinitely — until GitHub's runner-version deprecation floor
crossed the frozen version, at which point every listener exited at startup
with "Runner version vX.Y.Z is deprecated and cannot receive messages", the
units flapped into `start-limit-hit`, and jobs queued forever.

`plan` / `apply` now resolve the latest actions/runner release per arch and
classify any unpinned runner installed at an older version as a
recreate-class `runner_version` change, so a routine `ghars apply` keeps the
fleet current. If the releases API is unreachable, the plan degrades to the
previous installed-version behavior and carries a warning.

Also in this release:

- `apply` resets a unit's failed state (best-effort) before starting it, so
  recreating a fleet stuck in `start-limit-hit` does not have to wait out
  `StartLimitIntervalSec`.
- Work-dir disk growth on long-lived runners is bounded via a
  `JOB_COMPLETED` cleanup hook.
- Per-runner sccache server mode on shared cache pools
  (`server_mode = "per_runner"`).

## Assets

- `ghars-x86_64-linux-musl` — static (musl) x86_64 Linux binary.
- `ghars-aarch64-linux-musl` — static (musl) aarch64 Linux binary.
